title: Braised Beef Pot Roast with Root Vegetables
summary: A chuck roast is browned deeply then braised low and slow with onions, garlic and stock until it falls apart, with carrots and potatoes cooked right in the pot for a complete one-pan meal.
equipment: large heavy casserole (Dutch oven, 6 litres or more) with a tight lid

ingredients.item: boneless beef chuck roast (braising steak joint), tied
fine sea salt or table salt
large onions, cut into thick wedges
celery sticks, cut into 4 cm pieces
carrots, peeled and cut into 5 cm chunks
waxy or all-purpose potatoes, peeled and cut into 4 cm chunks
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Pat the beef dry and season all over with the beef salt and pepper. Heat the oil in the casserole over medium-high heat until shimmering, then brown the beef deeply on all sides, 10-12 minutes in total, before lifting it onto a plate — this deep colour is where most of the dish's savoury flavour comes from.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Turn the heat down to medium and cook the onions and celery in the fat left behind for 6-8 minutes, scraping the bottom of the pot, until coloured at the edges. Stir in the garlic, tomato purée and flour and cook for 2 minutes until the purée darkens slightly. Whisk in the stock and vinegar, scraping up every browned bit stuck to the base, then add the bay and thyme and bring to a simmer.

steps.title: Braise the beef
steps.text: Return the beef and its juices to the pot; the liquid should come about halfway up the sides. Cover with foil, then the lid, and braise in the oven for 2 hours 30 minutes, turning the beef once halfway through. A low, covered oven keeps the liquid just under a simmer, so the tough collagen in the meat melts slowly without the fibres drying out.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Tuck the carrots and potatoes in around the beef and sprinkle over the vegetable salt. Cover again and cook for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes more, until the beef yields completely when pressed with a fork and the vegetables are tender all the way through.

steps.title: Finish the sauce
steps.text: Lift the beef and vegetables onto a plate, then skim the fat from the braising liquid and discard the bay leaves and thyme stems. Boil the liquid for 5-8 minutes until it thickens slightly, then pull or slice the beef into large pieces and return everything to the pot with the sauce. Scatter over the parsley and serve straight from the pot.

tips: Don't rush the initial browning — a pale, under-seared joint gives a thin, flat-tasting sauce however long it braises afterwards.
Check the beef with a fork rather than a thermometer towards the end; it's ready when it pulls apart easily, not at a fixed temperature.
Keep the lid on tight during braising so the liquid stays at a gentle simmer rather than boiling hard, which can toughen the meat before it has time to soften.
Skim the fat from the sauce before serving, or it will taste greasy rather than rich.
storage: Keeps in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 3 days, or frozen for up to 3 months. Reheat gently on the stove or in the oven, covered, with a splash of stock if needed, until piping hot throughout (74°C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
